top_stories.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
top_stories.summary: A nation-state threat actor, Storm-0940, used an agentic AI tool called ARTEX to conduct a large-scale supply chain compromise via ConnectWise. The attack involved application credential abuse targeting Microsoft 365 environments, directly impacting identity and access security.

top_stories.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
top_stories.summary: Major tech platforms including Google, Mozilla, Apple, and the Go project blocked certificates from Indian Certificate Authority eMudhra after 8 cryptographic keys were found to be compromised. The affected certificates have been revoked, though the cause of the key compromise has not been determined.

top_stories.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
top_stories.summary: A webinar addresses the security risks posed by unmanaged AI agents operating within enterprise networks, specifically their unreviewed access to API keys, database passwords, and internal systems. The content focuses on AI agents as an emerging insider threat vector due to lack of identity ownership, access governance, and oversight—core IAM concerns around non-human identities.

top_stories.title: Best practices for integrating IAM Roles Anywhere with your PKI
top_stories.summary: AWS IAM Roles Anywhere allows workloads outside of AWS to obtain temporary credentials by integrating with a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). The article outlines best practices for this integration, covering credential security and access management for non-AWS workloads connecting to AWS resources.

top_stories.title: Corma Agents Automate Access Management Beyond API Limitations
top_stories.summary: Corma has launched browser-based AI agents designed to automate user provisioning and access workflows across applications, including those without provisioning APIs. The solution extends automated access management capabilities beyond traditional API-dependent methods for software license and access governance.

news.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
news.summary: Exaforce published an analysis of machine-speed attacks involving stolen GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers, and MFA phishing that can exfiltrate data within minutes. The report argues that faster automated detection and containment are necessary to counter credential theft and MFA bypass techniques.

news.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
news.summary: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher discovered that private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates were easily guessable and recoverable. The company's board made the decision five days after the vulnerability was reported, and eMudhra will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners.

news.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
news.summary: Railway, a PaaS provider, disclosed a security incident in which an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and in some cases obtained their decrypted contents. The company is urging credential rotation as the breach affects a subset of users whose stored secrets, such as API keys and passwords, may have been exposed.

news.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
news.summary: A vulnerability in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed malicious MCP servers to execute arbitrary code on a developer's Windows or WSL machine during the sign-in process. Anomaly patched the flaw in OpenCode version 1.18.33, with the exploit running under the developer's own access privileges.

news.title: From buzzword to blueprint: Implementing zero trust on Red Hat OpenShift with the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern
news.summary: Red Hat has published part 4 of a series on implementing zero trust security in OpenShift using the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern. The article focuses on making zero trust implementation repeatable within the OpenShift platform environment.

news.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
news.summary: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised in a supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and backdoor via PyPI wheels and Docker images. The package has since been quarantined on PyPI, with the attack documented by security firms SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Upwind.

news.title: eMudhra tanks 20%; why IT-enabled services stock sank in Wednesday's trade?
news.summary: eMudhra, a digital identity and certificate authority company, saw its stock drop 20% following reports of distrust of some of its intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs) used in its global TLS business. Certificate authority trust issues directly impact PKI-based authentication and identity verification infrastructure.

news.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
news.summary: A Dark Reading roundtable examined how AI is complicating identity security within the software development lifecycle. CISOs discussed that improved identity visibility and collaboration are key approaches to addressing identity gaps introduced by AI in development environments.

news.title: Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
news.summary: The article presents a reference architecture for securing AI agent identity using X.509 PKI, combining Keyfactor EJBCA and AWS services. The architecture incorporates signed request envelopes, delegation assertions, RFC 8693 audience-scoped tokens, and OCSP for cryptographic identity management in multi-agent AI systems.

news.title: Tools for Humanity Joins Zoom ISV Exchange Program; Expands Proof of Human Access to Zoom's Business Customers
news.summary: Tools for Humanity has joined the Zoom ISV Exchange Program, making World ID available in the Zoom Marketplace for enterprise customers. The integration provides human presence verification capabilities aimed at combating deepfakes in video communications, extending Tools for Humanity's biometric identity verification to Zoom's business user base.

news.title: Oak Research Finds More Than Half of Security Leaders Can't Fully See Who, or What, Has Access to Their Systems
news.summary: Oak released research showing that more than half of security leaders lack full visibility into who or what has access to their systems. The study highlights persistent gaps in identity governance including unreachable applications and ungoverned non-human identities, with AI agents identified as an emerging challenge.

news.title: CRM SSO: How single sign-on works in practice
news.summary: This article explains how single sign-on works within CRM systems, covering identity provider authentication and protocols such as SAML and OpenID Connect. The content appears to be an educational/explainer piece focused on CRM SSO implementation rather than reporting on new developments, research, or vendor news.

news.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled cloud backups after researchers identified attackers authenticating into Microsoft 365 tenants using ConnectWise credentials. ConnectWise states customer impact remains unconfirmed while the incident raises concerns about credential-based access compromise affecting downstream managed service providers.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: BeyondTrust's Remote Support product was hit by a zero-day vulnerability, joining Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks in a wave of exploited edge device bugs. BeyondTrust is a privileged access management (PAM) vendor, making this directly relevant to IAM security infrastructure.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. Security experts note that organizations are struggling to prioritize testing and deploying the volume of fixes, with Microsoft attributing the increased discovery rate to AI assistance.
